**Employment Type:**  

Full\-Time/Exempt **Wage:**  

$115,000 \- $125,000 base pay **Department:**  

Philanthropy **Reports To:**  

Director of Institutional Giving **Position Location**  

California – Oakland, Los Angeles, Sacramento, Riverside, Fresno **Work Schedule:**  

Four Day Work Week: Two (2\) days in office, two (2\) days remote. However, there may be certain circumstances, like pressing deadlines or peak business periods, where it becomes necessary for the organization to temporarily switch to a five\-day work week. **WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW**


California will define the next decade of climate action, and the resources behind that work have to keep pace. EnviroVoters is scaling its institutional funding program, and we need a senior fundraiser who can lead people, own strategy, and represent the organization with our most important foundation partners. This role sits at the center of a growing team, shaping how we cultivate funders, build the pipeline, and turn ambitious climate and justice campaigns into sustained investment.


This is a leadership role. The Deputy Director of Institutional Giving manages grant staff, drives portfolio strategy across both EnviroVoters (501c4\) and the EnviroVoters Education Fund (501c3\), and serves as a senior relationship holder with institutional funders. If you have led teams, closed six\-figure grants, and want your work to fuel real political power, we want to hear from you.

**What Makes This Role Distinctive**

* Four\-day work week for most of the year with five\-day weeks during peak periods
* Management of a growing institutional giving team, with authority to shape systems, strategy, and portfolio assignments
* Ownership of a portfolio of the organization's most significant institutional funders, with direct responsibility for cultivation, solicitation, and negotiation
* A leadership seat in departmental planning, revenue forecasting, and annual budgeting
* Dual\-entity fundraising across c3 and c4 structures, work that few institutional giving roles offer
* Comprehensive benefits package, including health, vision and dental coverage, 401(k) with employer match,12 days PTO, 12 holidays, a year\-end office closure between Christmas and New Year, and additional benefits that support employee well\-being and work\-life balance

**Position Summary**


As a senior member of the Philanthropy Team, the Deputy Director of Institutional Giving leads the day\-to\-day operation and growth of the institutional giving program for EnviroVoters and the Ed Fund. This role manages grant staff and consultants, owns a portfolio of high\-priority institutional funders, drives annual grant strategy and revenue planning in partnership with the Director of Institutional Giving, and ensures the full grant lifecycle runs with excellence across both entities.

**KEY PRIORITIES**

*Lead and develop the institutional giving team*

* Manage grant staff and consultants supporting the institutional giving portfolio, including hiring, coaching, and performance development
* Set portfolio assignments, workflows, and quality standards across proposals, reports, and stewardship activities
* Evaluate and strengthen systems and processes for grants management, ensuring compliance and alignment with organizational values

*Own strategic funder relationships*

* Manage a portfolio of the organization's largest and most complex institutional funders, leading cultivation, solicitation, negotiation, and stewardship
* Represent EnviroVoters and the Ed Fund with funders and program officers, including independently leading meetings, pitches, and site visits

*Drive portfolio strategy and revenue growth*

* Support in the execution of an annual institutional giving strategy aligned with organizational priorities and revenue goals
* Expand the funder pipeline by identifying, researching, and cultivating new institutional prospects for both entities
* Support the Director of Institutional Giving in annual budgeting, revenue forecasting, and monthly revenue reporting

*Ensure grant management excellence across both entities*

* Oversee production of multi\-year and one\-year proposals and reports, ensuring quality, accuracy, and timely delivery
* Provide internal guidance on permissible grant usage across c3 and c4 entities, including compliance with lobbying and electoral activity restrictions
* Project manage complex, cross\-departmental proposal development and ensure funding agreements are finalized, signed, and paid on schedule
* Work proactively with program, policy, and finance staff to meet all programmatic and fiscal reporting requirements

* Seven or more years of institutional fundraising experience in a nonprofit environment, including demonstrated success securing and renewing five\- and six\-figure grants
* Two or more years of staff management experience, with a track record of coaching and developing fundraising or grants professionals
* Expertise in cultivating and stewarding external funder relationships, including leading solicitations and negotiations independently

Job Description
An exciting opportunity to join the team of a progressive YMCA located in vibrant Somerset County, New Jersey. The YMCA is one of the nation’s leading nonprofit organizations dedicated to strengthening communities through youth development, healthy living and social responsibility. With a 150\-year\-old history, Greater Somerset County YMCA (GSCY) is a pillar of the community and has seven locations across three counties, which collectively serve upwards of 30,000 individuals. GSCY has 100 full\-time and 950 part\-time employees along with operating revenues to $22\+ million.


The Y empowers everyone—no matter who they are or where they are from. To fulfill our purpose of strengthening community for all, GSCY is committed to being an inclusive organization and leveraging our collective impact to address social inequities. To learn more about GSCY, visit our website: http://gscymca.org

**Job Description**
-------------------


NYC Department of Finance (DOF) is responsible for administering the tax revenue laws of the city fairly, efficiently, and transparently to instill public confidence and encourage compliance while providing exceptional customer service.
  

  

DOF’s Treasury and Payment Services Division is responsible for overseeing all City payment websites, the payment processing of tax returns, property recording forms, parking violation programs, and the collection of delinquent accounts, and oversees the agency’s management of the City’s cash balances and its relationships with banking institutions. Treasury and Payment Services is also responsible for collecting outstanding violations issued by City agencies and adjudicated by the Environmental Control Board.
  

  

Payments, Billing, and Refunds is responsible for processing payments for property taxes and property\-related charges, business and excise taxes, and parking and camera violations. The division is responsible for communicating amounts due, maintaining the quality of departmental records, and providing customer service to individuals seeking information on making payments or receiving refunds. Payments, Billing, and Refunds perform account adjustments and respond to refund inquiries from the public.
  

  

The Payment Technology unit seeks a thoughtful, dynamic, motivated individual, to serve as the CityPay Deputy Director of Data Analytics. With an interest in city government, the ideal candidate will use data to positively benefit the public. Additionally, the ideal candidate will use data to help inform and drive the decision\-making process, and inform strategies for efficient revenue collection, cost reduction, fraud mitigation, and predicting customer payment trends and behaviors. This position offers the opportunity to work with data analysts and staff across multiple City agencies and vendors.
  

  

Reporting to the Director of Payment Technology, the selected candidate’s duties and responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:
  

  

* Supervise and mentor interns and, potentially, junior data analysts in the unit, providing guidance and support in the areas of fraud analytics and other technologies related to operational data.
* Work closely with business owners and product managers to build and maintain ongoing analysis of their products, usage patterns and performance.
* Write database queries and code to analyze payment service usage volumes, user behaviors and performance data to identify opportunities and areas for improvement.
* Collaborate with other staff and analysts to create and maintain dashboards; where necessary and feasible, create and maintain other proprietary products for end users to fulfill specific business data service needs.
* Import data from external sources using Python scripting and export into formats that can be used for further manipulation by abroad set of division stakeholders with varying levels of experience, including executive staff.
* Create visual products such as charts, heat maps, and other visual infographics that illustrate data trends for a broad set of division stakeholders with varying levels of experience, including executive staff.
* Manage and maintain consolidated database of payments and transactional information from vendors, other business units, and legacy systems.
* Research, compile, investigate and analyze large quantities of data from a variety of sources, with an eye to identifying policy and operational implications.
* Communicate clearly and responsively your findings to a range of stakeholders, including management and executives.
* Develop key performance indicators and metrics for payment service delivery and products.
* Support current automated data processes and reports and develop automation for manual data processes.
* Recommend and implement improvements to collection, processing, flow and distribution of data.
* Document current procedures around data collection, processing and database management and editing.
* Administer a SQL Server Data Warehouse, gathering data from diverse platforms, such as Vendor Portals, FTP Servers, Oracle Production DB, and API calls.
* Develop and maintain scalable ETL pipelines on a RHEL (Red Hat Enterprise Linux) server using Python and shell scripts, with workflow scheduling and orchestration managed through cron jobs.
* Create and manage a Power BI workspace, design reports/dashboards for DOF Commissioner and senior management, and several other TPS units as well as other DOF units, and external agencies, including OMB. This tool has been heralded for providing intuitive insights into informed policy decisions.
* Collaborate with law enforcement agencies (local, state, federal)) to conduct ad hoc analyses, identifying and locating fraudsters on CityPay Site. Provided crucial clues and guided investigations effectively.
* Monitor and report on the performance of Fraud Detection technologies implemented on CityPay online and mobile platforms. (Ravelin, Fraud Detect, Account Validation, Blocked Plates etc.)
* Perform Quality Assurance (QA) processes for database testing, identifying data issues, and anomalies. Effectively communicate data scenarios to both business and technical teams, ensuring data accuracy and integrity.
* Develop predictive models utilizing machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help identify consumer payment and fraud patterns and trends.

**Compensation**

Immediate

About Kingdom Living Iowa \& RISE Recovery Center

Kingdom Living Iowa is a Polk County–based 501(c)(3\) nonprofit that has served Iowans in recovery since 2016\. We operate one of central Iowa's largest networks of recovery housing — 15 recovery residences — alongside RISE Recovery Center, a community hub offering peer recovery support, clinical care coordination, employment and family programming, and connection to every pathway to recovery. We welcome residents on medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) and are committed to keeping families together and honoring the dignity of every person in recovery.

About the Position

The Program Director leads **Key to Kinship**, a new family recovery housing initiative funded through Iowa HHS Opioid Settlement Funding. The program provides 30–90 day recovery housing vouchers and wraparound supports to families impacted by opioid use disorder (OUD) — with priority for pregnant and postpartum women with OUD and parents in recovery pursuing reunification with their children.

As the program's single dedicated leader, the Program Director runs the voucher program end to end: intake and eligibility, placement into MOUD\-supportive recovery housing, coordination of family supports, partner and case coordination, and full grant compliance and reporting. This is a hands\-on, mission\-critical role central to launching the program on time and to keeping Polk County families housed, stable, and connected to care.

Key Responsibilities

**Voucher Administration \& Finance**

* Oversee the recovery housing voucher system end to end, from referral through voucher exit.
* Manage the allocation and disbursement of funds for vouchers and secondary supports (transportation, infant and child necessities, employment coaching, family programming).
* Maintain a centralized financial ledger with quarterly compliance reconciliation.
* Monitor voucher utilization against the budget and adjust intake pacing to keep the program on track.

**Intake, Eligibility \& Clinical Coordination**

* Conduct intake screening, confirming OUD diagnosis or documented history of opioid use per grant eligibility requirements.
* Coordinate on\-site OUD/SUD clinical assessment and MOUD initiation or continuation through the clinical partnership with UCS Healthcare.
* Ensure naloxone (OORM) distribution and overdose\-recognition/response training for every participant and household at intake.

**Family Support Coordination**

* Coordinate delivery of wraparound supports that stabilize the whole family — transportation, infant/child necessities, employment coaching, and family programming through RISE Recovery Center.
* Conduct family needs assessments and lead quarterly case reviews with partners.
* Support custody and reunification milestones in coordination with Iowa HHS Division of Children and Family Services (DCFS) and the family court system.

**Strategic Partnerships \& Referrals**

* Serve as the primary liaison for referrals and joint case planning with clinical, treatment, housing, justice, and family\-service partners — including UCS Healthcare, ThriveNow Recovery Center, The Beacon, DART, Iowa HHS DCFS, family court, and Polk County corrections.
* Cultivate and maintain referral relationships to keep the program at capacity.

**Compliance, Data \& Reporting**

* Ensure strict adherence to all grant performance measures and Iowa HHS Opioid Settlement Funding contract requirements.
* Serve as the program's data steward: accurate, timely, and secure data entry and management in Airtable and FiveCRM, in full compliance with HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2\.
* Complete 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality training upon hire and annually thereafter, and ensure all staff with access to participant records do the same before handling protected substance use disorder information.
* Prepare and submit quarterly progress and outcome reports in IowaGrants and support monthly reimbursement claims.
* Monitor program fidelity benchmarks (housing stability, MOUD engagement, family reunification, voucher pacing) and trigger operational adjustments, partner consultation, and leadership reporting when thresholds are crossed.

**Housing Quality \& Program Integrity**

* Ensure voucher\-funded housing meets NARR certification standards and remains safe, stable, and recovery\-conducive.
* Uphold MOUD\-supportive, non\-discriminatory practice across all recovery pathways (MOUD, 12\-step, SMART Recovery, faith\-based, and holistic).

**Required**

* Bachelor's degree in social work, public administration, healthcare administration, counseling, public health, or a related behavioral health or human services field — **or** an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Minimum 2 years in a supervisory, coordinator, or program\-management role in behavioral health, family support, recovery services, social services, or a related field.
* Direct experience working with individuals or families affected by OUD, substance use disorders, or related behavioral health conditions.
* Experience with nonprofit financial oversight, grant compliance, data collection, or outcome reporting.
* Demonstrated ability to coordinate services across HHS, healthcare systems, community\-based partners, and family\-service systems.
* Strong organizational, communication, and documentation skills, with proficiency in data and case\-management systems.

About AlphaHire Intelligence
AlphaHire is a Workforce Intelligence Platform serving the construction, infrastructure, energy, power, and mission\-critical markets.


We help senior executives, private equity partners, operating partners, investors, developers, contractors, and project leaders answer a critical question before committing capital:

**Can this project, investment, expansion, acquisition, or growth strategy actually be executed?**


Our intelligence supports decisions connected to projects and investments frequently valued at more than $100 million.


AlphaHire evaluates the workforce and market conditions that can determine whether those decisions succeed, including:

* Workforce availability and capacity
* Compensation pressure
* Hiring competition
* Skilled\-labor constraints
* Project pipeline activity
* Infrastructure and power constraints
* Market saturation
* Contractor capacity
* Geographic expansion readiness
* Leadership and workforce concentration risk


We provide workforce and market intelligence that helps executives reduce execution risk before making major capital, expansion, investment, and operating decisions.


This position is exclusively focused on developing commercial partnerships for **AlphaHire Intelligence products and executive decision\-support solutions**. It does not involve selling recruiting or staffing services.


Our Research Ecosystem
AlphaHire’s intelligence capabilities are supported by a growing research ecosystem that includes the **Workforce Intelligence Lab** and the **AlphaHire Research Library**.


The Workforce Intelligence Lab is our nonprofit research organization focused on advancing workforce intelligence through original research, publications, fellowships, academic collaboration, grants, and institutional partnerships.


Our research ecosystem collaborates with multiple universities, academic faculty, research scientists, industry experts, and analytical partners. Research areas include:

* Workforce economics
* Labor\-market forecasting
* Infrastructure workforce capacity
* Compensation intelligence
* Labor shortages and hiring competition
* Construction workforce trends
* Workforce planning and execution risk


The AlphaHire Research Library brings together workforce studies, market intelligence, executive briefings, data, white papers, and industry research designed to support better executive decisions.


The Opportunity
AlphaHire is seeking a Director of Strategic Partnerships to build commercial relationships that expand the reach, distribution, and adoption of AlphaHire Intelligence across the United States.


You will identify organizations that already advise, influence, convene, or provide services to AlphaHire’s target buyers. These relationships may include referral partnerships, co\-selling arrangements, channel relationships, commercial research collaborations, data partnerships, enterprise distribution opportunities, and other revenue\-producing alliances.


Potential partners may include:

* Management consulting and advisory firms
* Private equity service\-provider networks
* Infrastructure and investment organizations
* Engineering, EPC, and professional\-services firms
* Construction and industry associations
* Economic\-development and site\-selection organizations
* Enterprise technology and data providers
* Research and market\-intelligence platforms
* Utilities, developers, and major project ecosystems
* Professional and institutional networks


Customer engagements produced through these partnerships typically range from approximately **$50,000 to $250,000** in first\-year contract value.

 **Requirements**  

* Identify and prioritize organizations capable of introducing, distributing, recommending, or co\-selling AlphaHire Intelligence.
* Develop relationships with senior executives, managing directors, partners, practice leaders, association leaders, and ecosystem decision\-makers.
* Build the strategic and commercial case for partnering with AlphaHire.
* Determine the appropriate partnership model, including referral, co\-selling, channel, distribution, research, data, or enterprise\-access arrangements.
* Lead initial partnership conversations and executive discovery.
* Qualify each organization’s buyer access, market credibility, commercial alignment, and revenue potential.
* Develop partnership proposals and activation plans with AlphaHire leadership.
* Negotiate commercial terms within approved parameters.
* Establish clear account ownership, referral attribution, opportunity\-registration, and communication processes.
* Convert partnership agreements into active introductions, qualified opportunities, and collected revenue.
* Coordinate partner\-enabled executive briefings, demonstrations, events, research discussions, and market initiatives.
* Maintain accurate records of partner activity, introductions, opportunities, and revenue.
* Monitor partnership performance and prioritize relationships producing measurable commercial outcomes.
* Represent AlphaHire accurately using approved positioning, research, and commercial materials.

  

**Benefits**  

This opportunity may be a strong fit if you have previously worked as a:

* Director of Strategic Partnerships
* Strategic Partnerships Executive
* Alliances Director
* Channel Sales Director
* Partner Development Director
* Ecosystem Partnerships Director
* Business Development Director
* Client Partner

jobs.description:
**Managing Director (Chief Operating Officer)**

Lead one of the country's most innovative animal welfare organizations. Help redefine what an animal shelter can be.

At Friends For Life, we don't simply rescue animals—we redesign systems.

We pioneered Houston's first no\-kill shelter, developed nationally recognized programs that keep pets with the families who love them, mentor shelters across the country, and continually ask a simple question:

How can we save more lives tomorrow than we saved today?

We're looking for an exceptional leader who thrives in fast\-moving environments, loves solving difficult problems, and believes compassion and accountability belong together.

This position isn't about maintaining the status quo. It's about helping build the future of animal welfare.

As Managing Director, you'll serve as the organization's operational leader, translating vision into execution while ensuring every department has what it needs to succeed. Working closely with the Executive Director, you'll oversee day\-to\-day operations, strengthen organizational systems, remove obstacles for department leaders, and ensure Friends For Life continues to innovate while remaining financially strong.

If you enjoy building teams, improving systems, making difficult decisions, and helping great people do their best work, we would love to meet you.

**What You'll Lead**

You'll directly supervise Friends For Life's Senior Leadership Team and other key staff members, including:

* Animal Pathways Director
* Animal Welfare Director
* Behavior \& Training Director
* Development Director
* Full\-Charge Bookkeeper
* Office Manager
* Volunteer Manager

**What You'll Do**

**Lead People**

Great organizations are built by great teams.

You will coach, mentor, and develop department leaders while creating a culture of trust, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. You will facilitate leadership meetings, conduct performance reviews, resolve conflict, and help every leader grow into the strongest version of themselves.

**Turn Vision Into Reality**

Ideas matter. Execution matters more.

Working alongside the Executive Director, you will translate organizational vision into measurable goals, priorities, and action plans. You will help departments establish meaningful metrics, monitor progress, and ensure every initiative moves Friends For Life closer to its mission.

**Build Better Systems**

You are energized by making organizations work better.

You will identify inefficiencies, remove barriers, improve workflows, and help create systems that allow our staff to spend less time fighting processes and more time saving lives.

You will cultivate a culture where problems are solved—not simply discussed.

**Protect Financial Health**

Mission success requires sustainability.

Working with the Executive Director, you'll oversee budgeting, financial planning, and organizational performance. You will participate in monthly financial reviews, analyze trends, monitor key metrics, and help ensure Friends For Life remains financially healthy while continuing to grow its impact.

**Drive Strategic Initiatives**

Some projects don't fit neatly inside one department.

You will lead cross\-functional initiatives, oversee strategic projects, coordinate implementation across teams, and ensure major organizational priorities are completed successfully and on time.

**Strengthen Communication**

Healthy organizations communicate well.

You will help ensure staff understand where the organization is headed, why decisions are made, and how every department contributes to our mission. You will facilitate quarterly State of the Organization meetings and foster an environment built on transparency, collaboration, and shared purpose.

**Keep Us Looking Forward**

Animal welfare continues to evolve.

So do we.

You will stay informed about emerging trends, encourage thoughtful innovation, evaluate new ideas using data, and help Friends For Life remain one of the industry's leading innovators.

**What Makes You Successful**

We're less interested in where you've worked than in how you lead.

You are someone who:

* Naturally develops leaders rather than simply managing employees.
* Makes thoughtful decisions, even when information is incomplete.
* Balances compassion with accountability.
* Loves solving complex operational problems.
* Thinks strategically while paying attention to details.
* Communicates with clarity, honesty, and empathy.
* Can juggle multiple priorities without losing sight of the mission.
* Builds trust quickly across teams.
* Remains calm under pressure.
* Enjoys continuous improvement and is not satisfied with "good enough."

**Qualifications**

Preferred qualifications include:

* Bachelor's degree in business administration, Nonprofit Management, or a related field.
* Significant leadership experience, preferably within nonprofit organizations or animal welfare.
* Experience overseeing budgets, financial planning, and organizational performance.
* Strong project management and organizational skills.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication abilities.
* Demonstrated ability to lead organizational change and build high\-performing teams.
* Creative, strategic thinking combined with strong execution.
* Passion for animal welfare and alignment with Friends For Life's mission.
* Knowledge of shelter operations, canine and feline behavior, or the animal welfare field is a plus.

**Working at Friends For Life**

Shelter work is meaningful, challenging, and sometimes unpredictable.

Everyone here is expected to pitch in wherever needed. While you'll have defined responsibilities, you will occasionally find yourself helping outside your department because that is what serving animals requires.

Some weekends and holidays are required.

**Compensation \& Benefits**

Salary: $75,000 annually

Benefits include:

* Paid time off
* Medical stipend
* Pet benefits

Take the next step in your career with this rewarding opportunity to join the YMCA of South Hampton Roads.
Job Description
Under the direction of Operations, the Senior Executive Director is responsible for the day\-to\-day operations and supervision of the assigned primary and secondary locations. This position provides Cause\-Driven leadership in staff supervision, volunteer management, fiscal management, financial development, membership and program administration, facility \& equipment stewardship, community relations and personal\-professional development. Qualifications
* Strong business operations background with a proven track record of producing growth and strong financial management
* Bachelor's degree in Human Services, Business Management, Business Administration, or equivalent
* Ten or more years of successful management experience, preferably in YMCA or other nonprofit agency in health and wellness field
* Must have previous experience working with diverse populations
* Supervision of full and part\-time employees with accountability of annual budgets
* Ability to establish and maintain collaborations with community organizations
* Ability to lead assigned operations including staff development and supervision
* Development and monitoring of budgets, membership and program development, financial marketing and public relations, board and volunteer development
* YMCA Multi Team Leader certification, preferred

* Requires ability to exercise appropriate independent judgement and make non\-routine decisions regarding day\-to\-day operational issues
* Requires effective team building and leadership skills
* Must maintain cooperative, functional relationships with senior leadership team, peers, and subordinates
* Must maintain a positive, energetic attitude toward YMCA work, goals and values
* Must have the ability to respond to emergencies 24 hours a day, and to travel as needed for operational management with on\-site presence managing major operational issues
* Must have superior oral and written communication skills and the ability to respond to a wide variety of constituencies, including staff, volunteers, members, program participants, vendors and community leaders
* Ability to perform the duties of direct reports as needed

**ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job


While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to:


* Physically able to successfully complete required job functions, including use of hands, arms, fingers, able to talk and hear, use a computer, sit and stand, regularly move/lift up to 50 pounds, enter all YMCA environments (office spaces, indoor and outdoor maintenance/mechanical areas, fitness areas, pool and pool space, camping areas, unimproved outdoor locations and other program areas)
* Continuous operations requiring attention to detail and multitasking
* Physically able to successfully complete required certifications

* Achieve budget expectations annually
* Meet quarterly and annual outcomes and expectations of the Association Strategic Plan
* Attain the Annual Campaign financial expectations
* Develop and grow the District programs and services in quality and quantity
* Supervision and maintenance (through partnership with Property Team) of two YMCA locations
* The development and leadership of exempt staff leaders

**Budget and Financial Performance**

* Develops, manages, and monitors center operating budgets to meet or exceed targets. Initiates and manages adjustments to the budget to assure a balanced operation and submits reports on current operations
**Program Development and Membership Engagement**

* Implements Association membership strategies that support the recruitment of new members and retention of existing members. Creates a member\-focused culture and models relationship\-building skills in all interactions. Uses YMCA "listen first" skills to understand and respond to the needs, wants, and interests of members. Fosters a climate of innovation and resolves problems to ensure member satisfaction
* Develops long\-range plans for the expansion of programs and services, in harmony with overall YMCA objectives. Monitors the achievements of these objectives and exercises appropriate action to assure the achievements of the objectives are of the highest quality programs and services
* Ensures safety, cleanliness and function of all related facilities and equipment
**Team Performance Toward Organizational Goals**

* Ensures all program operations are consistent with association procedures, including emergency, insurance, accident, purchasing, personnel, accounting and other administrative systems
* Recruits, hires, trains, develops and leads employees and volunteers. Reviews and evaluates performance.
* Develop strategies to motivate staff and achieve goals. Responsible for exempt staff and non\-exempt employees
**Fundraising**

* Provides leadership and is accountable for achieving the Annual Giving Campaign

* Communication and Influence
* Fiscal Management
* Engaging Community

jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

  


DREAM seeks a relationship\-driven, strategic, and collaborative **Director of Partnerships** to lead the development and stewardship of partnerships that support DREAM’s growth, programming, and long\-term sustainability.

  

DREAM relies on partnerships with affordable housing communities, housing authorities, schools, and other community\-based organizations to enter new communities and sustain our work over time. As DREAM continues to grow, partnerships beyond our core program sites are also becoming increasingly important to our operations, including relationships with summer meal providers, pools and parks, literacy organizations, camps, enrichment providers, and other community resources.



The Director of Partnerships will develop and implement a comprehensive partnership strategy across DREAM’s regions and programs. This position will cultivate relationships with affordable housing networks and management organizations, identify prospective program sites, steward existing partners, oversee partnership agreements, and help regional teams build strong and sustainable community connections.



The role will support partnership development for both DREAM’s Village Mentoring and Guided Mentoring programs while also building broader partnerships that expand opportunities and resources for young people. The ideal candidate has experience in affordable housing, community development, partnership management, or a related field and understands how to translate relationships into measurable organizational growth and impact.

 **Essential Functions**

  


Partnership Strategy and Growth


* Develop and implement an organization\-wide partnership strategy aligned with DREAM’s mission, programs, and growth goals.
* Create regional growth maps and conduct outreach to prospective partners in current and emerging regions.
* Establish annual partnership goals and track progress toward growth, stewardship, and renewal targets.
* Identify trends, gaps, and opportunities that inform DREAM’s regional and organizational growth strategy.


Housing and Program Partnerships


* Build and steward relationships with housing authorities, affordable housing organizations, property managers, schools, and community\-based organizations.
* Cultivate new partners that can support the expansion of DREAM’s Village Mentoring and Guided Mentoring programs.
* Represent DREAM within housing, education, community development, and nonprofit networks.
* Work with regional and program staff to assess prospective partners and determine readiness for new programming.


Partner Stewardship and Agreements


* Maintain strong relationships with existing partners through regular communication, recognition, reporting, and opportunities for feedback.
* Coordinate partner check\-ins, renewals, and follow\-up while supporting regional teams in navigating relationship challenges.
* Oversee the creation, execution, organization, and renewal of contracts, memoranda of understanding, and site agreements.
* Maintain centralized systems for tracking partnership contacts, commitments, agreements, deadlines, and next steps.


Community Resource Partnerships


* Develop partnerships that expand resources and opportunities for DREAM programs and youth, including summer meals, literacy programs, pools, parks, camps, transportation, and enrichment providers.
* Identify donated, discounted, or shared resources that strengthen programming and reduce costs.
* Help regional teams identify and cultivate local resource partners.


Collaboration and Reporting


* Serve as an organizational resource and provide tools, guidance, and training related to partnership development and stewardship.
* Collaborate with program, development, finance, communications, and regional teams to align partnership activities with organizational priorities.
* Maintain partnership records, prepare regular updates, and evaluate the effectiveness of DREAM’s partnership strategy.


**Qualifications**


* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.
* Two or more years of relevant experience in partnerships, affordable housing, community development, external relations, business development, or nonprofit leadership.
* Demonstrated success developing and sustaining external partnerships.
* Experience in affordable housing, including work with housing authorities, property management organizations, developers, resident services, or housing networks, strongly preferred.
* Experience developing partnership, outreach, or organizational growth strategies.
* Experience managing contracts, memoranda of understanding, or partnership agreements.
* Strong relationship\-building, communication, presentation, project\-management, and organizational skills.
* Ability to balance strategic planning with consistent follow\-through, documentation, and day\-to\-day relationship management.
* Experience working across multiple regions or with youth\-serving and community\-based programs preferred.
* Ability to travel periodically to DREAM regions and partner communities.


**Core Competencies**


* Relationship building and stakeholder engagement
* Partnership development and stewardship
* Strategic thinking and growth planning
* Knowledge of affordable housing and community systems
* Project management and follow\-through
* Cross\-functional collaboration
* Communication and problem\-solving
* Cultural humility and commitment to equitable community partnership


**Compensation**



Compensation for this position is based on experience, qualifications, and level of responsibility. DREAM is committed to internal equity and recognizes that candidates may bring varying levels of relevant expertise.



The anticipated salary range for this position is approximately $50,000–$70,000 annually, along with a comprehensive benefits package.

The Director of Development is responsible for implementing a strategy and building a pipeline that will grow to consistently produce gifts over $100k and being accountable for development outcomes by documenting and reporting on individual and team metrics.


Preferred candidates will have previous experience fundraising within higher education or a healthcare setting. They will demonstrate entrepreneurship and creativity in identifying prospects. A compelling candidate will have the desire to establish a foundation of excellence and will possess a proven record of meeting and exceeding goals and improving outcomes. They will also have demonstrated leadership skills and be able to create a highly stable and effective team by articulating clear goals and responsibilities and by providing feedback to support individual accountability.


**Responsibilities**


* Serve as the lead in\-market fundraiser for UVA Health managing a portfolio of donors and prospects. Identify, cultivate, solicit and steward these individuals in support of the mission and priorities of program leadership.
* In cooperation with the Executive Director, develop and execute a comprehensive fundraising strategy for UVA Community Health pulling from multiple prospect populations including patient families, community members, UVA friends and alumni, and beyond while serving as the lead fundraiser for community members and friends/alumni.
* Create and implement a transparent and intentional donor strategy to move prospective donors along the development continuum. Cultivate new and existing donors to higher levels of support for the departments and programs of oversight, including research and care of patients.
* Build and sustain collaborative, transparent relationships with in\-market providers in support of a grateful patient program.
* Evaluate HIPAA\-compliant patient data for physicians in assigned programs and identify potential major gift prospects for further research and cultivation. Ensure discipline around patient philanthropy processes as needed.
* Collaborate with UVA Health Development Office (UVAHD) colleagues to assure alignment and synergy in fundraising efforts. Work in tandem and in a donor\-centric manner to advance UVA Health broadly.
* Establish a consistent presence with volunteers and the community and promote a culture of philanthropy.
* Develop and maintain an informed layperson's understanding of the science behind the care delivered in\-market broadly. Act as a translator and synthesizer of ideas when needed to enhance communication for prospects/donors.
* Build and strengthen relationships with UVA and UVA Health leadership and key stakeholders as needed.
* Other duties as assigned.

  

The ideal candidate possesses excellent interpersonal skills, emphasizing collaboration, teamwork, and a solution\-oriented mindset, with exceptional oral and written communication abilities to convey information clearly across varying audiences. They demonstrate a strong customer service orientation, ensuring client satisfaction, and have a solid understanding of fundraising. With excellent organizational skills, keen attention to detail, and efficiency, they engage professionally with donors, volunteers, and stakeholders, maintaining confidentiality and discretion with sensitive information. Their strong critical thinking skills enable effective problem\-solving, and they adeptly prioritize tasks while adapting to shifting responsibilities.
